description:
List.reduce/3 gets two executable keys that differ only in the reducer's parameter type ({any, any} vs any). Both carry the same closure (#383) and the same captures. The two arrows are mutual subtypes (is_subtype both ways; canon_test.rs:44), yet ActivationKey::from_inputs (identity.rs:135) -> World::canonical_activation_key (world.rs:2833, 2846) / Types::activation_key_arrow keep the arrow's parameter, so one activation is compiled twice.

Reproducer (Optimize's scratch, on develop 56c37331e): repro/09999_dupkey_probe.fz and canon_test_probe.diff.

Blocks fz-sc8.192.3: its reds come from this duplicate. fz-engine measured that fz-9zq.17 does not clear them (independent). fz-engine suspects a shared root with fz-9zq.17 (both distinguish closure arrows differing only in a parameter, any vs {any, any}), and will measure one closure-arrow keying rule for both before building either.

Related, not identical: fz-t93.12 (same canonical text, distinct type ids).

User approved filing 2026-11-20 ("Proceed", relayed by Optimize). Owner: fz-engine.

Signal (from Optimize): the duplicate key on fixture 00567, and the Bag repro on plain develop (Optimize scratchpad walk/dev_probe.fz). Fixture 01068's List.reduce_cont/3 count going from 2 to 3 is NOT a symptom: the third key ([{any, any}], [], a2 -> r0) is a genuinely new input type, because Map.reduce now goes through List.reduce (rise approved by the user). A correct fix removes the 00567 duplicate and leaves 01068 at 3; 3 -> 2 is not success.
title: One activation has one executable key: equivalent closure arrows key alike
